relevance_note: Cohort of 7 children with SLE and lymphoproliferation in which one patient carries a TNFAIP3 variant: 'WES revealed a heterozygous c.559C>T (p. Q187X) mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene in patient 7'.
method_note: Hand extraction from the text; a short script only assembled the JSON. Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-4 are absent from the Markdown (only their titles are present), so per-patient table data (ages, individual features, laboratory values) could not be read; everything comes from the running text. Scope: of 7 enrolled patients only patient 7 carries a TNFAIP3 variant; patients 1-4 (somatic NRAS), 5 (no variant) and 6 (PIK3CD) are out of scope and get no rows. Relatives: the father is in scope because the variant 'is from her father' (he carries it; no phenotype stated). The grandparents were tested negative; the paper says only 'her grandparents', without number or side, so two rows ('grandparent of patient 7', 'grandparent of patient 7 2') were created as the minimum the plural implies; whether they are the father's parents is not stated, so the father's inheritance and parental-testing fields are left 'not reported'. Group statements: features stated for 'all patients' (SLE criteria, ANA, elevated IgG, hepatomegaly and/or splenomegaly and/or lymphadenectasis, no malignant marrow cells) and for 'these patients with mutations' with 6/6 counts (renal, hematologic involvement, recurrent fever) were applied to patient 7 as 'inferred from group statement'; patient 7 is one of the 6 patients with mutations (patient 5 had none). Counts below the group size (skin involvement 1/6, monocytosis in 'almost all') were not applied. Normal findings recorded per D-27: normal IgA, normal CD3+CD4+CD8- T-cell proportion and normal NK-cell numbers in patient 7 recorded as excluded abnormalities (reduced CD4 proportion and reduced NK cells chosen as the ruled-out abnormality because the paper contrasts them with 'reduced' in other patients). Checklist 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' marked observed from 'hematologic (cytopenia; 6/6 patients)'; the paper does not call patient 7's cytopenia autoimmune. Consanguinity recorded 'no' from 'No consanguinity was reported within the 7 families'. Variant type left 'not reported' (the paper never names the class). The patient was described previously (ref [18]). Contradictions noted (out of scope, NRAS): text gives c.38 A>G (p.G13C) while the Figure 2 legend gives c.38G>A, p.G13D; the abstract writes 'PI3CKD' for PIK3CD.
